opt_intro.message: All analysis runs locally in your browser. The only network requests are the optional lookups described below.

opt_intro_plain.message: Scam Detector checks pages on your own computer. It only contacts other services for the optional checks described below.

opt_plain_toggle.message: Non-tech terms: explain warnings in simple words

opt_plain_p.message: On by default. Turn it off to see the original technical wording (domain, RDAP, HTTP, favicon…).

opt_danger_label.message: Show the red "likely scam" banner at risk score ≥

opt_danger_label_plain.message: Show the red "likely scam" warning when the risk is at least

opt_warn_label.message: Show the amber "suspicious" banner at risk score ≥

opt_warn_label_plain.message: Show the orange "suspicious" warning when the risk is at least

opt_show_warn.message: Show the amber banner (the toolbar badge always shows the score)

opt_show_warn_plain.message: Show the orange warning too (the Scam Detector icon always shows the risk)

opt_rdap_toggle.message: Look up when a domain was registered (RDAP)

opt_rdap_toggle_plain.message: Check when each website was created

opt_rdap_p.message: Sends the site's domain name (never the full URL) to rdap.org, which redirects to the registry's public RDAP service. Results are cached for 7 days. Freshly registered domains are one of the strongest scam indicators, so this is on by default.

opt_rdap_p_plain.message: Sends only the website's name (for example example.com, never the full page address) to rdap.org, a public service that knows when websites were created. The answer is remembered for 7 days. Brand-new websites are one of the clearest signs of a scam, so this is on by default.

opt_feed_toggle.message: Keep a local copy of PhishTank's verified phishing reports and warn when a page or site is in it

opt_feed_toggle_plain.message: Keep a list of fake websites reported by PhishTank volunteers and warn me if I open one

opt_feed_p.message: A list of about 50,000 community-reported, verified phishing addresses is downloaded from data.phishtank.com a few times a day (about 2 MB each time) and stored on this device as hashes. Pages are matched locally: the addresses you visit are never sent anywhere. Reports are community data and are not guaranteed to be accurate.

opt_feed_p_plain.message: A list of about 50,000 fake websites, reported and checked by volunteers, is downloaded from PhishTank a few times a day (about 2 MB each time) and kept on this computer. Pages are compared here, on your computer: the websites you visit are never sent anywhere. The list is made by volunteers and may contain mistakes.

opt_feed_key.message: PhishTank application key (optional, raises the download limit; get one at phishtank.org):

opt_feed_key_plain.message: PhishTank key (optional, lets you download the list more often; get one at phishtank.org):

opt_sb_h_plain.message: Google's list of dangerous sites (Safe Browsing)

opt_sb_toggle.message: Also ask Google Safe Browsing about each page

opt_sb_toggle_plain.message: Also check each page against Google's list of dangerous sites

opt_sb_p.message: On by default, but nothing is sent until you enter your own API key below. With a key, the full address of every page you open is sent to Google's Safe Browsing Lookup service (create the key in Google Cloud, enable the Safe Browsing API and restrict the key to this extension). Google's terms allow non-commercial use only. Results are cached for up to 30 minutes.

opt_sb_p_plain.message: On by default, but it only starts working once you paste a free access key from Google below. With a key, the address of every page you open is sent to Google, which answers whether it is dangerous. To get a key, sign in to Google Cloud, turn on the "Safe Browsing API" and create an API key. Google allows this for personal, non-commercial use only. Answers are remembered for up to 30 minutes.

opt_sb_notice.message: Google works to provide the most accurate and up-to-date information about unsafe web resources. However, Google cannot guarantee that its information is comprehensive and error-free: some risky sites may not be identified, and some safe sites may be identified in error. Warnings based on this data are marked "Advisory provided by Google".

opt_sb_notice_plain.message: Google tries to keep this list accurate and up to date, but cannot promise it is complete or free of mistakes: some dangerous sites may be missed and some safe sites may be flagged by mistake. Warnings based on this list are marked "Advisory provided by Google".

opt_chat_toggle.message: Watch conversations on selling sites (OLX, Vinted, Wallapop, Leboncoin, Marktplaats, eBay, Facebook Marketplace, Idealista…) for known scam scripts

opt_chat_toggle_plain.message: Watch conversations on selling sites (OLX, Vinted, Wallapop, Leboncoin, Marktplaats, eBay, Facebook Marketplace, Idealista…) for known scam tricks

opt_chat_p.message: On by default. Chat text on those sites is checked locally (nothing is sent anywhere) for schemes such as "I'll send a courier, click the link to receive the payment", "forward me the SMS code", "the payment is held until you pay the insurance", "send the deposit before the viewing" or overpayment refunds, in English, Portuguese, Spanish and French. A banner explains the scheme when one appears.

opt_chat_p_plain.message: On by default. Messages in chats on those sites are checked on this computer (nothing is sent anywhere) for common tricks such as "I'll send a courier, click the link to receive the payment", "forward me the SMS code", "the payment is held until you pay the insurance", "send the deposit before the viewing" or paying too much and asking for the difference back, in English, Portuguese, Spanish and French. A warning explains the trick when one appears.

opt_brands_p.message: One per line: Brand name | keyword1, keyword2 | realdomain.com, other.com. Keywords are matched inside hostnames; real domains are never flagged. Useful for your bank, employer or local services.

opt_brands_p_plain.message: One per line: Brand name | word1, word2 | realwebsite.com, other.com. If a website address contains one of the words but is not one of the real websites, you are warned. Useful for your bank, employer or local services.

chat_courier_pickup_title.message: Buyer wants to send a courier and pay remotely

chat_courier_pickup_advice.message: Classic OLX/Vinted scam: the "courier" or "delivery service" is fake and the payment link steals your card details. Only use the platform's own delivery and payment flow.

chat_courier_pickup_advice_plain.message: A well-known scam on selling sites: the "courier" or "delivery service" is fake and the payment link steals your card details. Only use the selling site's own delivery and payment.

chat_payment_link_title.message: Asked to open a link or enter card details to "receive" money

chat_payment_link_advice.message: Nobody needs your card number, CVV or a link to pay you. Real platform payouts go to the account you already set up. Do not open the link.

chat_payment_link_advice_plain.message: Nobody needs your card number, the 3 digits on the back of your card or a link to pay you. Real payments from the selling site go to the account you already set up. Do not open the link.

chat_fee_to_release_title.message: Payment "held" until you pay a fee or insurance

chat_fee_to_release_advice.message: Money that is "blocked until you pay insurance / transport / a verification fee" does not exist. The fee is the scam.

chat_sms_code_title.message: Asked to forward a verification code

chat_sms_code_advice.message: The code is being used to take over an account (WhatsApp, Google Voice, the marketplace itself) in your name. Never share codes you receive by SMS.

chat_sms_code_advice_plain.message: With that code, the scammer can take over one of your accounts (WhatsApp, Google Voice, the selling site itself) and pretend to be you. Never share codes you receive by text message.

chat_overpayment_title_plain.message: Paid too much and asks for the difference back

chat_overpayment_advice.message: The original payment is fake or will be reversed; any "difference" you send back is lost.

chat_abroad_title.message: Counterpart claims to be abroad / unable to meet

chat_abroad_advice.message: Buyers or sellers who "cannot come in person" and will handle everything remotely are a common scam setup. Prefer in-person handover or the platform's delivery.

chat_off_platform_title.message: Pushing the conversation off the platform

chat_off_platform_title_plain.message: Wants to move the chat to another app

chat_off_platform_advice.message: Scammers move to WhatsApp, Telegram or email so the platform cannot see or block them. Keep the conversation and the payment inside the platform.

chat_off_platform_advice_plain.message: Scammers move to WhatsApp, Telegram or email so the selling site cannot see or block them. Keep the conversation and the payment on the selling site.

chat_pay_first_title.message: Payment demanded upfront through an untraceable channel

chat_pay_first_title_plain.message: Asks you to pay first in a way that cannot be traced

chat_pay_first_advice.message: Deposits by bank transfer, MB WAY, Bizum, PayPal "friends and family", gift cards or crypto before you have the item cannot be recovered. Use the platform's protected payment or pay on collection.

chat_pay_first_advice_plain.message: Money sent before you have the item, by bank transfer, MB WAY, Bizum, PayPal "friends and family", gift cards or crypto, cannot be got back. Use the selling site's protected payment or pay when you collect.

chat_rental_deposit_title.message: Rental: deposit requested before any viewing

chat_rental_deposit_advice.message: Never pay a deposit, "reservation" or first month before visiting the property and meeting the landlord. Keys "sent by courier" or payments "handled by Airbnb/Booking" for a classified ad are a scam.

chat_fake_payment_proof_title.message: Fake payment confirmation or "upgrade to receive"

chat_fake_payment_proof_advice.message: Screenshots of "completed transfers" are easily faked, and no bank or platform requires a business account or an upgrade to receive a payment. Check your own account balance, not their screenshot.

chat_pressure_advice.message: Urgency is used to stop you from thinking. Take your time and verify.

chat_phishing_link_advice.message: "$1" is not a real $2 address. Opening it will lead to a fake payment or login page.

chat_external_link_title.message: External link sent alongside payment or delivery talk

chat_external_link_title_plain.message: Link to another website sent while talking about payment or delivery

chat_external_link_advice.message: Links to $1 should not be needed to pay or ship. Stay on the platform.

chat_external_link_advice_plain.message: You should not need a link to $1 to pay or send an item. Stay on the selling site.

welcome_caution_h.message: Please read: this tool cannot catch every scam

welcome_caution_p1.message: Scam Detector looks for the signs that known scams leave behind. It will miss some scams, and it will most likely miss new tricks that nobody has spotted and described yet.

welcome_caution_p2.message: So do not trust it blindly. No warning does not mean a site or a message is safe. Stay alert, and never enter passwords, card numbers or codes when something feels off.

welcome_what_p.message: Every time you open a page, Scam Detector checks it on your computer for warning signs: a website created only days ago, an address pretending to be a bank or a well-known brand, a page asking for your password or card on the wrong website, and wording typical of scams (prizes, urgent payments, "pay a fee to receive your money"). If the risk is high, a warning appears at the top of the page.

welcome_badge_h.message: The colour of the Scam Detector icon

welcome_badge_yellow.message: Yellow: a few small warning signs. Click the icon to see them.

welcome_badge_red.message: Red: a warning is showing on the page. Be very careful.

welcome_badge_grey.message: Grey with a check mark: a website you chose to trust.

welcome_badge_neutral.message: Not checked yet (for example a browser page): blue-grey.

welcome_chat_p.message: On sites such as OLX, Vinted, Wallapop, Leboncoin or Facebook Marketplace, Scam Detector also reads the conversation and warns you about well-known tricks, like a "courier" who will pay you through a link, or a request to forward a code you received by text message.

welcome_privacy_p.message: Pages and chats are checked on your computer. Only the name of each website (never the full address or what is on the page) is sent to a public service to learn when the website was created, and a list of reported fake websites is downloaded a few times a day. If you add your own Google key in the settings, page addresses are also checked with Google's list of dangerous sites.

welcome_settings_p.message: You can change all of this, and switch between simple and technical wording, in the settings.
